title: FIFA visits Nigeria as NFF reform intensifies
seoTitle: FIFA visits Nigeria amid NFF reform efforts
subtitle: With the NFF in crisis, FIFA and CAF send mission to Abuja seeking solution
excerpt: FIFA and CAF travel to Abuja to assess the NFF's situation after the board's resignation and the threat of international sanctions.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Daily Post Nigeria, Sports247 Nigeria, Vanguard News
contentHtml:
The crisis in the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has gained international attention after FIFA sent an email confirming a visit to the country to assess the situation, following the resignation of the NFF board.

FIFA and CAF Send Joint Mission to Abuja

In an email dated September 7, official Elkhan Mammadov, FIFA's Head of Member Associations, stated that the organization and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) would conduct an assessment mission in Abuja. The objective is to gather information from stakeholders and analyze the legal, governance, administrative, and electoral implications of the crisis.

Officials' Reaction and Point of Contact

FIFA requested that lawyer Emmanuel Ikpeme serve as the main point of contact between the NFF, FIFA, and CAF, replacing the National Sports Commission (NSC) until further notice.

Former Players' Expectations for the Reform

Former Super Eagles midfielder, Friday Ekpo, emphasized that the reform must go beyond administrative changes and regain fan support. For him, the success of the reform will be measured by the return of spectators to stadiums, competitiveness in continental competitions, and qualification for major tournaments.

President Tinubu's Guidelines for the Reform

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has ordered a comprehensive reform encompassing governance, development pathways, domestic competitions, stakeholder representation, and accountability. FIFA and CAF's participation in the discussions is anticipated.

Challenges Highlighted by Analysts

Experts warn that the reform cannot merely be a change of names. An independent audit is needed to examine the entire system, from the NFF's legal structure to the management of finances, contracts, grassroots development, referees, and player welfare. They also emphasize the importance of preventing the federation's autonomy from turning into impunity.

NFF's Next Steps

The NFF has suspended the September elective congress and established an interim arrangement under the leadership of Emmanuel Ikpeme to maintain essential operations while consultations continue with FIFA, CAF, the government, and other stakeholders.

With information from Daily Post Nigeria, Sports247 Nigeria, Vanguard News.
